title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: About 492 ships are now waiting outside Hormuz, and only 101 escorted transits got through in three days last week. Riyadh airport reopened on Sunday, and UAE airlines have set Saudi return dates between 30 October and 8 November, so road into KSA stays the main route for another one to two weeks.

gauges.note: As of 25 Oct; about 194 off Fujairah and Khor Fakkan (JMIC via Gulf News)

stories.headline: Nearly 500 ships are queuing outside Hormuz
body: About 492 vessels were waiting outside the strait on 25 October, says the Joint Maritime Information Center. Roughly 194 are near Fujairah and Khor Fakkan and 178 off Dubai. Only 101 US-facilitated transits went through between 22 and 24 October, against a normal 138 or so a day. UAE officials have not confirmed the figures.

What is new since Friday: an LPG tanker was hit by a projectile near Limah, Oman, on 22 October, and oil from a tanker damaged earlier reached the Umm Al Quwain coast on 23 October. Iran's IRGC says two supertankers hit mines on 23 October; this has not been independently confirmed. JMIC rates the threat in the strait as severe.
stories.soWhat: The east-coast queue is now the bottleneck. Quote Khor Fakkan and Fujairah inbound with longer, buffered transit times, not prewar ones.

stories.headline: Riyadh airport reopens; UAE airlines set Saudi return dates
body: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh resumed operations on 25 October after a two-week closure. Terminal 1 handles domestic flights and Terminal 2 international flights by Saudi carriers.

UAE airlines are coming back slowly. Emirates resumes Jeddah on 30 October and Riyadh and Dammam on 8 November. flydubai returns to Riyadh, Dammam and Abha from 30 October. Etihad stays off Riyadh and Dammam, and some Jeddah flights, until 5 November. Air Arabia has no return date. The risk has not gone: Saudi forces intercepted a Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh on 24 October.
stories.soWhat: New today: firm restart dates. Belly space into KSA stays thin for one to two more weeks, so keep selling road and plan for air volumes to swing back from 8 November.

stories.headline: Air rates jump again as jet fuel doubles
body: The Baltic Air Freight Index rose 4.7% in the week to 19 October and is 26.4% higher than a year ago. Rates from Europe to the UAE rose further.
Jet fuel was 113.7% higher year on year to 16 October, per IATA's monitor.
stories.soWhat: Our air costs are rising with the market. Check that fuel surcharges pass through in full and do not discount air going into peak.

stories.headline: UAE and Greece sign €12.75 billion of deals, including ports and logistics
body: The UAE–Greece Strategic Forum in Athens announced 18 MoUs, agreements and partnerships worth €12.75 billion in total. Sectors include logistics, transport and ports, along with energy, AI, healthcare and food security.
No separate figure or project was given for logistics.
stories.soWhat: A possible new Europe gateway for UAE trade. Watch for named port or corridor projects before we build a product around it.

competitors.name: DHL Express
competitors.headline: Adds a Saudi domestic demand surcharge from 1 November
body: DHL will charge SAR 0.40 per kg on Time Definite Domestic shipments in Saudi Arabia from 1 November to 31 December. Its international demand surcharge, running 1 October to 5 February, is SAR 0.50 per kg within MENA and SAR 6.40 per kg from China and Hong Kong into MENA.
DHL says amounts and dates may change with prior notice.
competitors.soWhat: The market leader is pricing peak into KSA domestic. That gives us cover for our own peak surcharge in Saudi, and a price point to stay under.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: Launches dangerous-goods road service across five GCC markets
body: FedEx now carries eligible dangerous goods by road between the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman. The Regional Economy and Regional Economy Freight services take parcels and pallets: lab reagents, diagnostic samples, dry ice, chemicals and lithium batteries.
Trucks run from its Dubai World Central hub on a TIR-registered, GPS-tracked fleet, with ADR-aligned handling.
competitors.soWhat: FedEx is going after healthcare and battery freight on the same roads we sell into KSA. Check our DG road offer and price it before FedEx signs our healthcare accounts.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Saudi belly space returns from 30 October; freighter fleet keeps growing
body: Emirates resumes Jeddah on 30 October and Riyadh and Dammam on 8 November, ending the suspensions that had SkyCargo trucking its Saudi backlog.
SkyCargo expects 23 dedicated freighters by end-March 2027 and has added seven 777 freighters since March. Its freighter network grew from about 40 to over 60 destinations between March and July.
competitors.soWhat: Our road edge into KSA has a clock on it. Lock shippers into road contracts now, before Emirates belly space comes back.
competitors.imageCredit: Emirates SkyCargo via Air Cargo News

opportunities.title: Road into KSA for two more weeks
opportunities.text: Emirates is out of Riyadh and Dammam until 8 November and Etihad until 5 November. Air shippers still need road express and FTL.

opportunities.title: Dangerous goods by road
opportunities.text: FedEx's launch shows demand for DG road freight in the GCC. Healthcare and battery shippers will compare offers now.

opportunities.title: Saudi peak pricing
opportunities.text: DHL adds SAR 0.40/kg on Saudi domestic from 1 November. There is room for our own peak surcharge below that.

opportunities.title: East-coast handling
opportunities.text: About 194 ships wait off Fujairah and Khor Fakkan. Shippers will pay for drayage, storage and clearance help there.

opportunities.title: Firm air yields
opportunities.text: Global air rates are up 26.4% on last year and jet fuel has doubled. No reason to cut air prices.

watchouts.title: Possible US strike on Iran
watchouts.text: A US envoy said a strike was possible last weekend; Trump said not on 25 October but did not rule one out. Escalation would hit Gulf air and sea again.

watchouts.title: Houthi missiles at Saudi
watchouts.text: A missile aimed at Riyadh was intercepted on 24 October, and debris injured two people in the south on 25 October. Saudi restart dates could slip.

watchouts.title: East-coast queues
watchouts.text: Nearly 500 ships wait outside Hormuz. Khor Fakkan and Fujairah delays will keep growing.

watchouts.title: Air volume swings back in November
watchouts.text: When Emirates returns on 8 November, some road volume to KSA will move back to air. Do not over-commit truck capacity past that date.

watchouts.title: UPS results on 27 October
watchouts.text: Watch for comments on Middle East surcharges and peak pricing.

moves.title: Sign road shippers into KSA contracts before 8 November
moves.text: Offer 4–8 week road rates to accounts that moved from air, so they stay with us when Emirates belly space returns.

moves.title: Set a KSA domestic peak surcharge
moves.text: Benchmark against DHL's SAR 0.40/kg from 1 November and price just under it.

moves.title: Price a DG road product for healthcare accounts
moves.text: Check our ADR coverage on UAE–KSA–Oman lanes and quote healthcare and battery shippers before FedEx does.

moves.title: Re-set east-coast inbound transit times
moves.text: Add buffers on Khor Fakkan and Fujairah quotes and offer storage and drayage as paid add-ons.

moves.title: Audit air fuel surcharge pass-through
moves.text: Jet fuel is up 113.7% year on year. Make sure every air contract passes it on.

moves.title: Plan the air restart into KSA
moves.text: Book capacity with Emirates and flydubai for 30 October to 8 November restarts and tell customers the dates.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
